name: riskrails
description: A weight-based engineering pipeline for Claude Code and Codex: each change is weighed on six axes, runs light, guarded or full, edits only the files its plan names, and ends at human approval — enforced by hooks, reviewed adversarially, routed to the cheap model tier by default.

interface.shortDescription: Weight-based engineering pipeline with enforced scope and cost-aware model routing.
interface.longDescription: Installs one dual-runtime module: an .ai/ engineering pipeline shared by Codex and Claude Code, agents rendered for whichever runtime you use, and three hooks that enforce the rules mechanically rather than by asking politely. Every change runs discovery → context → impact → risk tier → plan → implementation → test → adversarial review → security review → release report → human approval, with the stages scaled to the tier and none of them skipped. Each implementation step names the files it may touch and anything else is refused, including inside a multi-file apply_patch. Routine workload stays on the cheap tier; the expensive tiers are spent only on a named trigger, and a bundled zero-cost usage report shows where the tokens actually went. No agent merges or deploys; commit, push and approval run only as the command the human picked in the dialog, or the human runs them outside the agent.
capabilities: Run a change through a risk-tiered pipeline with the gates its tier requires
Refuse edits outside the current approved step, file by file
Block force pushes, history rewrites, protected-branch pushes and secret staging
Survey an existing production codebase into a reusable .ai/ knowledge base
Audit a repository against the twelve plays of the AI-native SDLC
Report token usage and cost from local transcripts at zero model cost
interface.defaultPrompt: Set up RiskRails in this repository with /rr-setup, then run my next change through /rr-build.
